title: Canary Autoscaling Safety Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a cross-cutting approach for running safe canary rollouts in private deployments (VPC / on-prem clusters) where autoscaling policies interact with release signals. It is intended as a practical reference for SREs, platform engineers, and release owners who need to ensure SLAs are preserved while enabling progressive delivery and fast rollback.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: Kubernetes clusters managed via ArgoCD (App-of-Apps), Helm charts for Redwood services, and Terraform for cloud/VPC infra and cluster autoscaling modules.
- Image provenance: we require signed images (cosign) and optional attestation before promotion to canary and prod.
- Observability: metrics collected via Prometheus + tracing and a runbookable alerting layer in PagerDuty.
- Network: private clusters may have constrained egress; preflight steps include local mirrors for images and attestation tokens.

High-level goals:
1) Prevent cascading scale events triggered by canary traffic that would violate cluster-level CPU/GPU quotas or increase customer costs unexpectedly.
2) Ensure canary traffic exercises the same autoscaling code paths as production but with bounded resource and time budget.
3) Automate gating (smoke tests, SLO checks, attestation) where safe, but always provide a clear manual abort path.

Playbook overview (phased):
Phase 0 - Preflight (CI/CD and TF module readiness)
- Validate Terraform autoscaling modules: ensure modules expose a "canary" scaling profile and a safe lower-bound replica count. Example variables: canary_min_replicas, canary_max_replicas, burst_target_pct.
- Terraform pattern: prefer a separate ASG/VMSS (or node pool) typed for canary workloads to isolate scheduling and quota. Module notes: tag nodepool with "rw-canary=true" and expose taint/toleration defaults for Helm.
- Confirm image signing: pipeline must produce a cosign signature and push an attestation to the registry. For airgapped clusters, sync signed images to the local registry and copy signatures.
- Generate an immutable release tag (release/<sha> or semver) and create an ArgoCD App with the canary overlay (kustomize or Helm values file).

Phase 1 - Canary deployment with autoscaling guardrails
- Deploy into a canary nodepool with constrained resources and a horizontalPodAutoscaler that is limited by a hard max_replicas_canary variable.
- Configure HPA targetCPU (or targetGPU-util) conservatively to avoid immediate scale-up: start with a target at 60% and use scale-up stabilization windows of 2m.
- Use PodDisruptionBudget that permits safe rollout while protecting minimum capacity.
- Helm values example (note: keep in values.yaml):
  canaryEnabled: true
  canary.nodeSelector: { "rw-canary": "true" }
  canary.tolerations: "[\"key=canary,operator=Exists,effect=NoSchedule\"]"
  canary.hpa: { minReplicas: "2", maxReplicas: "6", targetCPU: "60" }

Phase 2 - Traffic shaping and smoke testing
- Ramp traffic to canary using the ingress/sidecar routing layer. Prefer request sampling rather than full % splits when possible. Example: start at 1% for 10 minutes -> 5% for 15 minutes -> 25% for 30 minutes.
- Run automated smoke tests after each step: end-to-end latency check, token-cost regression test, and a quality sampling job (5 example prompts). Smoke test runner returns pass/fail and details.
- Monitoring gates (examples):
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5m -> fail
  - 95th latency increase > 30% relative -> fail
  - Error budget burn > 10% in 15m -> fail
- If metrics approach thresholds, pause traffic ramp and wait for manual review.

Phase 3 - Autoscaling interaction validation
- Observe nodepool autoscaler react: ensure it scales nodes but respects cluster quota. Recommended signal capture: HPA desiredReplicas, kube-scheduler pending pod count, cluster-autoscaler scale events.
- Look for oscillation signals: repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down within 5-10 minutes indicates instability. If observed, reduce canary traffic and set HPA stabilizationPolicy to longer windows.
- Cost guard: the canary nodepool should have a billing tag and a budget alert that triggers if cost delta > X during the experiment (typical X = 15% of expected).

Phase 4 - Promotion or rollback
- Promotion criteria: all smoke tests pass AND no busy signals (no oscillation, and metrics within thresholds) for a sustained window (default 30m). Also verify image attestation exists in registry for the promoted tag.
- Promotion action: update ArgoCD root App to use the release tag and trigger progressive rollout to production nodepools.
- Rollback action: ArgoCD rollback to previous Git commit + mark image in registry as revoked (cosign revocation record) and run a quick sweep to remove canary images from local caches.

Runbook snippets (common commands)
- Check ArgoCD health and resume/abort:
  argocd app list --project private-deploys
  argocd app sync redwood-service-canary --prune --retry
  argocd app rollback redwood-service-canary 1

- Inspect HPA and pods:
  kubectl -n redwood get hpa redwood-service-canary -o wide
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-service -o wide

- Verify cosign signature (example):
  COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign verify --key <kms:key-uri> ghcr.io/redwood/service:release-2024-11-02

Terraform module patterns (notes for maintainers)
- Module split: cluster + nodepools + autoscaling-policies as separate modules. Provide a small wrapper that composes these for each environment.
- Expose canary profile variables in the autoscaling module and default them to conservative values. Document them in README with examples.
- Provide an output: canary_nodepool_id and canary_taint_key for Helm values injection.
- Example var names: canary_nodepool_name, canary_min_size, canary_max_size, canary_node_labels.

Airgapped considerations
- Signed image sync: push cosign signature files and OCI index to the local registry. Store signatures in the same namespace as images and maintain an index to avoid lookup failures.
- If attestation verification is unavailable due to offline KMS, maintain a local allowlist for a short time window with an explicit operator approval flow. Record approvals in the release Git commit message.

Postmortem and telemetry
- Capture experiment metadata in a canonical experiment log: release_tag, canary_traffic_profile, start/end timestamps, smoke test hashes, final decision, and owner.
- When things go wrong, ensure the postmortem references the experiment log and the Terraform plan used for nodepool changes.

Open questions and next steps (action items)
- (Maya) Draft a small terraform wrapper module that creates an isolated canary nodepool and exposes taints/labels by 2024-11-22.
- (Sofia) Prototype a low-friction cosign cache sync flow for airgapped registries and document in the private-deployments Confluence.
- (Arjun) Create a gating lambda that aggregates smoke results and auto-pauses ArgoCD promotions if a gate fails.

Appendix: quick checklist for an on-call engineer
- Confirm that the release tag has a cosign signature accessible from cluster registry.
- Ensure the canary nodepool has been created and shows Ready nodes.
- Start at 1% traffic, run smoke suite, check gates.
- Watch HPA desired vs actual and cluster-autoscaler events for the first 30 minutes.
- If aborting: cut traffic, ArgoCD rollback, run cosign revoke procedure, notify release owner.

This document is intentionally pragmatic and mutable — please copy into a working release playbook and iterate based on observed failures in early experiments.
